endpoints.summary: Send direct debit authorization to a Customer
endpoints.description:
No required attributes to be passed.

This call will send an e-mail to the customer with a request for an authorization payment,
typically 1 or 2 cents, in order to be able to direct debit the customer. Only when the customer
pays the authorization payment the direct debit for this customer is enabled.
If so the Customer mollie_direct_debit_status will be mollie_direct_debit_accepted
and it will have a mollie_mandate_id.

endpoints.description:
Creates a new Expense for the current organization.

The expense_type field accepts cost, income, or balance.
Note: bedrijfsmiddel type is not supported via this API.

The delivery_period is required for cost and income expense types.

ledger_account_id comes from GET /v3/ledger_accounts/expenses/cost,
/income or /balance, whichever matches expense_type.

raw_total_amount is signed by the direction the money moves: a cost is
negative and income is positive, and a balance expense follows the side
of the ledger account it is booked on. A credit invoice inverts that, so a
credited cost is positive and credited income is negative. Every vat_amount
has to carry the same sign as raw_total_amount. The expense is read back
with the sign it was given, and so is the payment registered against it
through POST /v3/payments/register.

endpoints.description:
Reports the revenue and the costs booked in a period, and the profit that follows from them.

Give year on its own for the whole calendar year, year and quarter for one quarter of it, or
year and month for one month of it. quarter and month cannot be combined. Reporting runs
from 2006 up to and including the year after the current one, since bookings can be dated ahead of
today; a year outside that range is rejected.

Pass label_ids to report only the bookings carrying one of those labels; the identifiers are
the ones returned by GET /labels. Give more than one comma separated,
label_ids=<id>,<id>.

The report is split into five sections, keyed by the Dutch names jortt books them under:
opbrengsten (revenue), kosten (costs), resultaat_uit_deelnemingen (result from
participations), buitengewone_baten_en_lasten (extraordinary income and expenses) and
winstbelasting (profit tax). A section that holds nothing over the period is left out, so
expect between zero and five of them. The side of a section is the side it is booked on,
which is also what says whether it adds to the profit (credit) or subtracts from it
(debit).

Every amount is an amount and the side it stands on together, and the amount itself is
never negative, so nothing has to be read against a sign convention. A section usually stands
on the side it is booked on; one that was credited back more than it was booked -- a period
whose only booking on a cost ledger is a correction, for instance -- stands on the other side.
possible_profit is revenue minus costs, profit_before_tax corrects that for the two
sections in between, and profit is the result after profit tax; a profit stands on the credit
side and a loss on the debit side.

The ledger_accounts of a section are the section's tree of ledger accounts flattened depth
first: every account is followed by the accounts booked under it, which depth and
parent_id spell out, and accounts sharing a parent come in descending order of the absolute
value of their amount. An account with nothing on it and nothing under it is left out; one
whose own amount is zero because the accounts under it cancel each other out stays, so a
parent_id always names an account that is in the list.

endpoints.description:
Reports the assets, the liabilities and the equity of the organization as at the end of a period.
Unlike the profit and loss report this is a position on a single date rather than a sum over the
period, and as_of_date states which date that is.

Give year on its own for the whole calendar year, year and quarter for one quarter of it, or
year and month for one month of it. quarter and month cannot be combined. Reporting runs
from 2006 up to and including the year after the current one, since bookings can be dated ahead of
today; a year outside that range is rejected.

Labels cannot be applied to this report: a balance filtered by label would no longer balance.

Each item is keyed by the Dutch name jortt books it under, such as balans_vorderingen
(accounts receivable) or balans_liquide_middelen (cash and cash equivalents), and says which
side of the balance it is listed under -- debit for the assets, credit for the
liabilities and the equity -- and which group within that side it belongs to. total_debit
and total_credit are always equal. An item holding nothing is left out, as is a ledger
account with a zero position, and what remains comes in the order of the balance: the assets
first, the liabilities and equity after them.

Every amount is an amount and the side it stands on together, and the amount itself is
never negative. An item usually stands on the side it is listed under; one holding a position
that belongs on the other side of the balance, such as a loss under balans_onverdeelde_winst,
stands on that other side.
